visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A woman with long brown hair, wearing a black T-shirt featuring a Beethoven portrait, stands centrally against a neutral, beige-toned studio background. (2) A digital graphic overlay appears covering the top half of the screen, showing the header of a scientific journal article from the "Journal of Hospital Infection." The text is clear and formal. The woman remains visible in the lower half, pointing upwards towards the text. (3) The scene cuts to a close-up visual of a pair of hands with darker skin tones washing a thick, orange-colored cleaning cloth. The cloth is being squeezed and rubbed within a yellow plastic basin filled with white soapy bubbles and water. The background is blurred. (4) The video returns to the previous medium shot of the woman in the black t-shirt. She continues her explanation, now clasping her hands together and then spreading them apart. The background features a warm lamp light and a dark shelf with a small object. (5) A new graphic overlay is displayed, showing a different research paper title regarding "Microfiber Pollution." It includes icons of a washing machine and clothing. The woman is partially visible underneath the text, continuing her narrative with focused facial expressions and small hand movements. (6) The final phase shows the woman leaning slightly forward towards the camera. She points her finger for emphasis. Variety-style text captions with slashes like "\媽你看到了嗎\" appear briefly at the bottom, styled differently from the standard white dialogue subtitles seen throughout the video.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to educate viewers about the hygiene and environmental trade-offs between using reusable cleaning cloths (rags) versus disposable paper towels, using scientific research as evidence to suggest that paper towels might be a more hygienic and surprisingly environmental choice in certain contexts.
